authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 135.1 aṅguli explicitly gives Maithili ā̃gur, Nepali aũlo and Lahnda aṅgal “finger”. The Maiya agui-type form is separately listed under 135.2 *aṅgūḍi and is assigned there; opaque reduced or retroflex-r forms remain distinct audit questions. Reviewed comparison: awan aŋgal “finger” (f_vkincccfs5b52). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

These ending-bearing forms select kaṇṭaka, not bare kaṇṭa. Reviewed comparison: kaithal kanḍa “thorn” (f_ya5wtcyviqrss). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10978 lavaṇa gives the widespread loṇ/lūṇ salt family. Regional retroflex initial ḷ and the northern retained-v lovn do not require a different lexical root; their phonetic details remain in the source transcription. Reviewed comparison: awan lū̃ṇ “salt” (f_ajp6ntdbib6om). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 9349 bhaginī gives Bshk-area bai(n), Kashmiri biñ, Punjabi bhaiṇ and regional bahin/bheṇ “sister”. Simple n-retaining variants can be linked provisionally; additional r in baharṇ requires a separate morphological account. Reviewed comparison: KochariyaEastDanuwar bahin “younger sister” (f_oynxmtz5wr43a). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 7655 pañca explicitly gives Dardic panž/panz and Pashai paĩ/paẽ, alongside Kalasha poñ and Shina poĩ. The survey affricate-to-sibilant and contracted nasal/glide numerals fit this documented five family; exact local phonetic developments remain qualified. Reviewed comparison: Buksa pãntʃ “five” (f_rr5qoqwidwmsw). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 12598 śṛṇoti explicitly gives Bhojpuri sunal and western suṇṇo “hear”. Eastern -l and western -y inflections can continue the hear stem; sun-lo and ambiguous sunā causative/past forms require local morphology. Reviewed comparison: awan sū̃ṇ “(you) listen” (f_p72kkhymlacti). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
